lines.text: Chapter seven, section one. Overview and objectives.
The last chapter looked at c-betting when you did not have a range advantage; this chapter looks at the mirror image, defending when you actually do.
The defender who has a stronger range than the pre-flop aggressor can take a big share of expected value, but only if she plays actively.
Passive defense, just calling and hoping to bluff-catch, leaves money on the table when the range dynamics favor you.
By the end of this chapter you should be able to identify the flops where the pre-flop caller has an equity or nut advantage.
You should be able to convert that advantage into a real check-raising range, with clear value hands and well-chosen bluffs.
You should be able to plan turn and river follow-ups so that your check-raise is not a one-street bluff but a multi-street threat.
And you should be able to attack thin c-bets from the aggressor, punishing the over-frequency mistake that many players make in these spots.
